author: Mon
text:
[Investigation & fix proposal]

Root cause
On iOS, KakaoTalk's in-app browser is a WKWebView, and iOS blocks Universal Links when triggered from inside another app's WKWebView. So links in Kakao messages stayed on the web page instead of opening the app. Android already works because it uses the Android intent:// scheme. (The iOS redirect path in our code was also left disabled.)

Chosen approach (frontend-only, no native/template change)
Inside the iOS Kakao in-app browser, hand the link off to the external browser (Safari) via KakaoTalk's openExternal scheme. Once in Safari, our existing Universal Link / AASA setup opens the installed app, and falls back to web/App Store when not installed. This avoids needing a new iOS custom URL scheme and avoids re-registering Kakao templates (the App Link "AL" button alternative).

Implemented in apps/legacy-mobile/.../common/services/universal-link.service.ts (covers both message buttons and inline links; Android unchanged).

Remaining dependency / risk

* Behavior of kakaotalk://web/openExternal can vary by KakaoTalk version -> must be verified on a real iOS device before closing.
* Universal Link only fires on a domain in the app's Associated Domains — please confirm with the App team which domains (e.g. m.ohmyhotel.com, dev domain) are associated.
* Promotional / Event (친구톡) messages are sent outside oh-api -> need to confirm those links also route through a Universal-Link domain to be fully covered.

author: Daniel
text:
Dear @Justin ,
Following the Phase 0 survey of the ELLIS Admin read APIs, here are the findings and decisions for the six open items.

1. Does an OpenAPI/Swagger spec exist? Effectively no — not for the APIs in our scope. A springdoc/Swagger setup exists, but it only covers a small number of public channel-facing APIs, not the internal admin read APIs the MCP server needs. So for the admin endpoints there is no usable auto-generated contract; they will need to be documented manually.

2. API auth method (API Key / JWT / OAuth)? ELLIS does not use OAuth. The admin APIs authenticate via a session token passed in the userToken header (server-side session). Implication: the MCP server must provide its own auth at the boundary and call ELLIS using a dedicated read-only credential, rather than relying on a standard OAuth/JWT flow from ELLIS.

3. Is there a staging/dev environment (no direct PROD)? Yes — dev, test, and local environments are available. Phase 0 validation will target these; no direct PROD access.

4. Response format, pagination, rate limits? Response format: every response is wrapped in BaseDtoV2Rs (succeedYn flag + errorCode + result). The MCP layer must unwrap result and map succeedYn/errorCode to tool errors (business failures still return HTTP 200). Pagination: list endpoints paginate by limit/offset and return TOTAL_COUNT. Rate limit: QPS rate limiting exists only for the partner flow, not for the admin flow => MCP server must enforce its own rate limiting / output caps.

5. Source endpoints for the 4 v1 tools. list_channels/get_channel: POST /admin/user/comp/seller; get_settlement: POST /admin/settlement/seller; get_mapping_status: POST /admin/hotel/code-mapping; margin (channel detail): POST /admin/hotel/markup/item. All POST with request body, not REST GET. Detailed request/response field mapping per tool still to be confirmed in tool stories (ELS-2032-2035).

6. Does ELLIS support per-user / row-level authorization? No. ELLIS does not enforce per-user or row-level authorization for internal admin staff. => The entire RBAC layer must be built at the MCP level; it cannot be delegated to ELLIS. This makes ELS-2029 heavier in scope than a simple pass-through.

Summary: Items 1-4 characterize API behavior, item 5 maps tools to source endpoints, item 6 defines the authorization gap. These close the Phase 0 pre-requisites and unblock the scaffold (ELS-2026), RBAC (ELS-2029), and the four tool stories (ELS-2032-2035).

One open point: what format and level of detail would you like for the API inventory (e.g. per endpoint: request/response fields, source service/table, sample payload)? Best regards, Daniel

author: Justin
text:
@Daniel, First, thank you for the thorough survey — having all six items answered closes the Phase 0 gates. You're the PIC on this, so treat everything below as a starting point rather than a fixed spec: if you see a better fit or better tool design, propose it and push back.

Please structure the inventory per MCP tool (the 4 v1 tools), not per endpoint, so each entry drops straight into a Spring AI @Tool definition. Three blocks per tool:

A. MCP contract — follows the MCP standard (2025-11-25 Tool specification): name/title/description, inputSchema (JSON Schema), outputSchema (JSON Schema), annotations. Map ELLIS field names+types onto the drafted input/output sets (ELS-2032-2035). For annotations suggest readOnlyHint=true, idempotentHint=true, openWorldHint=false as defaults; annotations are hints not enforcement — real read-only/RBAC enforcement is server-side via read-only scoped credential + ELS-2029.

B. ELLIS source binding (core): endpoint (method+path) and request body; response DTO -> output fields after unwrapping BaseDtoV2Rs; source service/table; pagination (limit/offset/TOTAL_COUNT); error mapping (succeedYn=false/errorCode -> tool error isError); one sample request + one redacted sample response.

C. Governance (first-cut proposal as PIC, finalized in ELS-2029 RBAC / ELS-2030 audit-masking / ELS-2031 PII-rate-caps): which fields are PII/sensitive + suggested masking; draft RBAC scope per tool (e.g. get_settlement=finance-only, KR/VN separation) and where MCP-side filtering is needed; observed result sizes and suggested output/rate caps.

Field-level detail required for input/output. Two things to capture: (1) list_channels and get_channel share POST /admin/user/comp/seller — split list vs detail projection; (2) get_channel composes two endpoints (seller detail + /admin/hotel/markup/item for margin) — show how they combine. Format: no Confluence — write as Markdown (.md) attached to ELS-2025. Best regards, Justin

author: Daniel
text: Dear @Justin , Thank you — this is very clear, and I've got all of it. As PIC I'll follow the structure exactly as you laid out: Inventory per MCP tool (4 v1 tools), three blocks each — A. MCP contract (MCP 2025-11-25 spec: name/title/description, inputSchema, outputSchema, annotations readOnlyHint=true, idempotentHint=true, openWorldHint=false), B. ELLIS source binding (endpoint, request/response field mapping after unwrapping BaseDtoV2Rs, source service/table, pagination, error mapping, one sample request + redacted response), C. Governance (PII/masking, draft RBAC scope per tool, suggested output/rate caps). I'll split list_channels vs get_channel as distinct list/detail projections, and show how get_channel composes the two endpoints. Field-level JSON Schema for input/output, only exposed fields plus source mapping. Delivered as Markdown .md attached to ELS-2025 so ELS-2032-2035 can reference it. For block C I'll give a first-cut proposal, finalize together in ELS-2029/2030/2031. Best regards, Daniel

author: Harry
text: Hi @Justin, Thanks for the priority bump and the scaffold. The host-keyed manifest + fm-route detect/PR governance + pc/mobile=cloudfront, hana=nginx wiring is exactly the right shape. PR: github.com/ohmyhotelco/ohmyhotel-monorepo/pull/80. 4-item update: 1. get-distribution-config.json captured — distribution E2GG6OCG9J158 (Comment Ohmyhotel-web), single origin pointing at legacy ALB prd-ohmyhotel-alb-746667910.ap-northeast-2.elb.amazonaws.com. 2. drift-check CI job — will add next. 3. route-flip.md live-apply TODOs — will fill with captured ID + ETag re-fetch step. 4. www and m share E2GG6OCG9J158 — one distribution with both as aliases; manifest needs reshape (single-distribution-keyed or host-keyed-with-caveat). 3 surprises in live config: 1. /build/* behavior already exists — points at legacy ALB with CachePolicyId 658327ea (Managed-CachingOptimized); flipping = update existing behavior's TargetOriginId. 2. Session token storage and transport are two separate things — storage key window.location.hostname+'_userToken' in localStorage; transport reads token and attaches lowercase header usertoken; CloudFront forwards userToken header and Cookies.Forward=none. Recommend option C dual-write for v2 SSR auth: legacy+v2 write to both localStorage AND cookie; SSR reads cookie for first-navigation auth-gated rendering, localStorage survives payment redirect cycles. Dual-write is permanent shape not transitional. Not needed yet for static/CMS pages — lock in before Phase 2 (OMH-457). Post-close finding on OMH-652 D1: merged Dockerfile ships build/client/ in the image; during rolling deploy old task renders HTML referencing entry.aaa.js while new task only has entry.bbb.js -> 404 -> UI breaks. S3 day-one closes the gap; revised architecture on branch as docs/migration/cloudfront-s3-ecs-architecture.md. Ping me on: (a) manifest shape, (b) /build/* origin (S3 vs Fargate), (c) confirm option C dual-write before Phase 2. Thanks.
